source.author: hor
source.text: si fractus illabatur orbis, inpavidum ferient ruinae.
source.text_original: si fractus illabatur orbis, / inpavidum ferient ruinae.
source.text_english: If the broken world should collapse, its ruins would strike him unafraid.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: uix barbarorum effugerat manus et auulsas de complexu suo uirgines fleuerat, cum subito intolerabili et quod numquam timuerat amantissimi filii orbitate percutitur et quasi futura uirginis Christi auia spe futurorum mortiferum uulnus excepit probans in se uerum esse, quod in lyrico carmine super iusti praeconio dicitur: si fractus illabatur orbis, inpauidum ferient ruinae.
reuse.text_original: uix barbarorum effugerat manus et auulsas de complexu suo uirgines fleuerat, cum subito intolerabili et quod numquam timuerat amantissimi filii orbitate percutitur et quasi futura uirginis Christi auia spe futurorum mortiferum uulnus excepit probans in se uerum esse, quod in lyrico carmine super iusti praeconio dicitur: si fractus illabatur orbis, inpauidum ferient ruinae.
reuse.text_english: She had scarcely escaped the hands of the barbarians and wept over the virgins torn from her embrace, when suddenly she was struck by the unbearable bereavement of her most beloved son, a loss she had never feared, and, as though by the hope of being the future grandmother of a virgin of Christ, she received the deadly wound, proving in herself the truth of what is said in the lyric poem in praise of the righteous man: if the shattered world should fall in, the ruins would strike him unafraid.
